issues.description: Class name mismatch between the UML in the problem statement and the provided code: the UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares the class as 'Course' (UML class declaration at problem_statement.md lines 63–63), while the template implementation declares 'public class Lecture' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java in the template at line 3) and the reference solution also declares 'public class Lecture' (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java at line 3). This inconsistency can confuse students about which class to implement and where to add the specified attributes and methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the UML diagram in problem_statement.md to use 'class Lecture { ... }' so the diagram matches the exercise text, the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java), and the solution. Alternatively, if 'Course' was intended, rename the provided Java files and update the exercise text and tests to use 'Course' consistently.
